chunks: And in the narration of Ḥarīz, from Zurārah, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, he said:

When the Day of Resurrection comes, Allah will establish the proof against seven: the child, the one who died between the prophets, the very old man who lived to the time of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم while not comprehending, the simple-minded, the insane one who does not comprehend, the deaf, and the mute. Each one of them will present an argument before Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

He said: Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will send to them a messenger, who will kindle for them a fire and say: Indeed your Lord commands you to leap into it. Whoever leaps into it, it will be coolness and peace upon him; and whoever disobeys will be driven to the Fire.

key_terms.احْتَجَّ: established the proof or argument decisively
key_terms.الطِّفْلِ: the child, one not yet fully accountable
key_terms.النَّبِيِّينَ: the prophets, referring here to the interval between prophetic missions
key_terms.الْأَبْلَهِ: the simple-minded person lacking normal discernment
key_terms.بَرْدًا وَسَلَامًا: coolness and peace, meaning harmless safety in the fire
key_terms.سِيقَ إِلَى النَّارِ: driven to the Fire as punishment
key_terms.يَوْمُ الْقِيَامَةِ: the Day of Resurrection, when final judgment takes place

ai.seo_question: How will those who lacked full understanding or access to divine guidance be judged on the Day of Resurrection?
ai.summary: This hadith describes a trial on the Day of Resurrection for those whose worldly circumstances prevented normal accountability, such as children and those lacking comprehension. It portrays Allah’s proof and justice being established through a command, after which obedience leads to safety and disobedience leads to the Fire.
